name: cavemio-csv-import
title: CSV import
description: Contacts → Import, done properly: your file's columns thread themselves to your fields, bad cells become fields you fix in place, and the rows go to your server in batches.

cavemio.accessibility:
- The drop target is the label of a real file input: Tab reaches it, Enter or Space opens the picker, and its focus ring shows on the target.
- Matching works without a pointer: every field's pill opens a listbox (arrows, typing a name, Enter), and clicking a column then a field matches them too. Threads are drawn for the eye; screen readers hear the pills.
- Problem cells are real inputs marked aria-invalid with their reason under them. The import bar is a progressbar with the row counts as its values. Each step's result is announced in a status region.
- Nothing leaves the browser until onImport: parsing, matching and checking all happen on the page.
- Reduced motion swaps steps in place and draws threads and checks at once.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: fields
props.description: – · { key, label, required?, match?, validate? }. match lists other column names to recognise; validate returns why a value won't do.

props.name: onImport
props.description: – · Saves one batch of rows shaped { [key]: value }. Return failed: [{ index, reason }] for rows your server refused; throw to mark the whole batch skipped.

props.name: maxRows
props.description: 50000 · Files with more rows are refused before matching.

props.name: noun
props.description: { one: "row", many: "rows" } · What a row is, for the counts and buttons.

props.name: templateHref
props.description: – · A "Download a template" link under the drop target.

props.name: onDone
props.description: – · After the last batch, e.g. to refresh the list behind it.

props.name: ref
props.description: – · load(text, name?) reads text as if it were a dropped file, e.g. from a paste or a sample.

features.title: Big files don’t freeze the page
features.description: The file is read in slices with a pause between them. 200,000 rows take about a quarter of a second.

features.title: Columns match themselves
features.description: Columns that match a field by name, ignoring case and punctuation, are already threaded. Carry a column onto a field, or use its dropdown, to change it.

features.title: Checked before anything is sent
features.description: Every row is checked first, and the counts read like “2,996 ready · 4 need a look”.

features.title: Fix problems in place
features.description: Rows with problems open with their bad cells as fields. Fix one and it folds away, or skip what is left.

features.title: Sent in batches
features.description: Rows go to your onImport function in batches with a progress bar. Cancel stops after the batch in flight.

features.title: Skipped rows come back as a CSV
features.description: Anything skipped or refused downloads as a file with the reason on each row.

states.title: drop
states.description: Dragging a file over the target turns its edge blue and lifts the icon 4px with a slight overshoot; the line morphs to "Drop to read it". A file that isn't CSV, is empty or is over maxRows shakes the target and says why.

states.title: read
states.description: The file is parsed in 200,000-character slices with a pause between (200,000 rows take about a quarter of a second), the icon spinning. The separator is taken from the first line.

states.title: match
states.description: Steps slide in 28px from the right while the card eases to its height. Columns that match a field by name, ignoring case and punctuation ("E-mail address" → Email), are threaded on arrival; each thread draws itself in 520ms. Carrying a column trails a dashed thread and lights the field under the pointer. Each field's pill grows into the list of columns, a sample under every name; narrow cards show only the fields and their pills.

states.title: review
states.description: Every row is checked (required fields, then validate). The ready and need-a-look counts roll. Rows with problems show their bad cells as inputs with a red thin line and the reason; when a row is right its badge morphs to Fixed, and 650ms later it folds away.

states.title: import
states.description: Ready rows go to onImport in batches of batchSize. The bar fills by transform; the count rolls. Cancel aborts the signal and stops after the batch in flight. A batch that throws marks its rows as skipped with the error's message.

states.title: done
states.description: A ring draws in 640ms, then a check. If anything was skipped or refused, "Skipped rows" downloads them as CSV with a column saying why.
